account:
Today I have been keeping my scheduled appointments: office correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, and town accounts. During the market walk, several townsfolk reported that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That seems consistent with ordinary baking supplies; I have no evidence of anything unusual about it. I inspected the treasury and found 128 emeralds, withdrawing none. The secretary says no accounts have been brought to her and has recorded that balance.

The unresolved matter is my three o'clock tea appointment. The appointment book specifies tea with a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank, but names neither the neighbour nor a particular cottage. The secretary took the book for safekeeping and investigated. She reports that the cottages were unanswered and warehouse workers knew nothing, so neither host nor cottage is confirmed. She has now offered to accompany me to the dockside to seek the neighbour. This looks like an inadequately specified social appointment, though I do not yet know who arranged it or its purpose beyond tea. I have seen no evidence of a hidden scheme or other unusual town activity.
